entries.definition: (of speech) heavily and noticeably regional
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A speech word: it grades how thickly the regional colouring comes through, not how plainly a thing shows itself.

entries.definition: easily seen or detected
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Near-instrumental in feel — it frames the thing as something a look or a test turns up, where *perceptible* frames it as something the senses take in.

entries.definition: capable of being seen or noticed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The most guarded of the three — it grants only that the thing can be picked out, without *evident*'s suggestion that it announces itself.

entries.definition: capable of being seen or noticed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Stronger than *discernible* on the same footing: what is evident presents itself rather than waiting to be made out.
examples: a clearly evident erasure in the manuscript

entries.definition: strongly marked; easily noticeable
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Raises the degree rather than the ease — the thing stands out by how strongly it is set off, not by how little effort finding it takes.

entries.definition: capable or worthy of being noticed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain, unjudged term of the set — it rates a thing as able or worth noticing without saying whether the noticing is welcome, which is exactly what *obtrusive* adds.
examples: noticeable for its vivid historical background

entries.definition: capable of being seen or noticed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flattest of the three — a bare statement that observation is possible, carrying none of *evident*'s force.

entries.definition: undesirably noticeable
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The one member that judges: it puts the noticing at the top of the scale and calls it unwanted, where *marked* only measures how far the scale runs.
examples: the obtrusive behavior of a spoiled child

entries.definition: easily seen or detected
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Pitches the same easy visibility at the observer's senses rather than at a search, which is what sets it apart from *detectable*.
examples: he continued after a perceptible pause

entries.definition: strongly marked; easily noticeable
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Carries the same heightened degree as *marked*, but with the sense of a quality pushed forward until it cannot be missed.

entries.definition: capable of arousing and holding the attention
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The hold is inward and quiet, attention drawn in rather than seized as by *gripping*.

entries.definition: providing enjoyment; pleasantly entertaining
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm and easy - the praise is for the pleasure given, not for any grip on attention of the kind *gripping* asserts.

entries.definition: providing enjoyment; pleasantly entertaining
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The stiffer, more formal shape beside *amusing*, claiming the same pleasure with less warmth in the saying.

entries.definition: providing enjoyment; pleasantly entertaining
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Understated praise - the enjoyment is framed as a pleasant turning-aside, milder than *amusing*.

entries.definition: capable of arousing and holding the attention
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Stronger than *absorbing*: attention is not merely drawn in but wholly occupied, with nothing left over.

entries.definition: agreeably diverting
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Light approval - it promises agreeable diversion rather than the deep hold *engrossing* claims.

entries.definition: capable of arousing and holding the attention
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The hold works like a spell - attention is charmed into staying rather than pinned there as by *riveting*.

entries.definition: capable of arousing and holding the attention
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Physical in its force - attention is taken hold of rather than invited, where *fascinating* wins it.

entries.definition: arousing or holding the attention
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The flattest word here - it grants that attention is held and says nothing about how hard, which *absorbing* and *riveting* both do.

entries.definition: capable of arousing interest or curiosity
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The pull is curiosity rather than pleasure - it promises something not yet given, where *fascinating* holds you with what it shows.
examples: our team came up with some most intriguing finds

entries.definition: sufficiently interesting to be reported in a newspaper
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A threshold rather than a compliment - it measures whether interest clears the bar for reporting, where the rest of the family reports the pull itself.

entries.definition: capable of arousing and holding the attention
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The most immobilising of these - attention is fixed in place, not merely drawn in as by *absorbing*.

entries.definition: no longer in your possession or control; unable to be found or recovered
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flat, final member - it puts a thing beyond holding and beyond recovery both, naming a deprivation rather than a mishap.

entries.definition: lost temporarily; as especially put in an unaccustomed or forgotten place
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Gentlest here - the thing is still somewhere, merely not where it was put, so the loss is provisional and faintly self-excusing.
examples: the mislaid hat turned up eventually

entries.definition: lost temporarily; as especially put in an unaccustomed or forgotten place
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The same provisional loss as *mislaid* in a flatter, more formal register, faulting the position a thing ended up in rather than the act of setting it down.

entries.definition: not able to be found
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Pure report of absence - it says only that the thing cannot be found, and unlike *lost* leaves recovery open.

entries.definition: not used to good advantage
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The condemning member - what was had was spent to no purpose, and the word insists someone did the spending.

entries.definition: (of an animal) having no home or having wandered away from home
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Of an animal, it makes homelessness a settled condition rather than an incident, carrying pity and a touch of nuisance at once.

entries.definition: unable to find your way
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Names only the predicament of being unable to find your way - a passing disorientation beside the standing state *stray* describes, with no blame in it.

entries.definition: not used to good advantage
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Registers value come to nothing without fixing on a culprit, which is the accusation *squandered* adds.

entries.definition: devoid of significance or force
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A deflating verdict rather than a scornful one, saying only that nothing of weight is there and leaving the sneer to *vacuous*.

entries.definition: devoid of significance or force
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The outward form is intact and the inside is not, so it carries a ring of sham that flat *empty* does not.

entries.definition: signifying nothing
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A cool dismissal of what a thing stands for rather than of its size or loudness, drier and less final than *nonsensical*.

entries.definition: having no meaning or direction or purpose
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Plain on the surface and bleak underneath, since it withholds direction and purpose along with sense, condemning where *nonmeaningful* only records.

entries.definition: lacking the thinking capacity characteristic of a conscious being
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Descriptive rather than damning in this sense, stating an absence of thinking capacity without laying blame, where *nonsensical* passes judgement on what was produced.
examples: the shrieking of the mindless wind

entries.definition: having no meaning or direction or purpose
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Colourless and technical, it notes the absence and adds no dismay to it, where *meaningless* sounds the loss.

entries.definition: having no intelligible meaning
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunt and unadorned, refusing the thing any intelligible sense without softening the refusal.

entries.definition: having no intelligible meaning
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The fuller, more formal judgement that nothing can be made of the thing at all, weightier in the mouth than blunt *nonsense*.

entries.definition: without meaning
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plainest statement in the family, that meaning is simply absent, with none of the scorn *vacuous* or *nonsensical* carry.
examples: Silence is better than unmeaning words

entries.definition: devoid of significance or force
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The withering member of the three: formal, and it treats the missing force as a fault rather than a fact.

entries.definition: deliberately arranged for effect
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the deliberation and no more — the effect was composed, which is a fact before it is a complaint.

entries.definition: contrived by art rather than nature
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The family's flat baseline: it says a thing was contrived rather than grown and stops there, where *unreal* goes on to deny it.

entries.definition: having particular physiological functions augmented or replaced by electronic or electromechanical components
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Strictly technical — it reports function augmented or replaced by machinery and carries none of the deficiency the rest of the family hangs on the made.

entries.definition: (used of color) artificially produced; not natural
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Colour got by stripping rather than adding, and the word keeps the drained, washed-out feel of that.

entries.definition: without substance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Withering — the thing is flat, propped up, and has nothing behind it.

entries.definition: artificial as if portrayed in a film
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Gives the thing the sheen of a screen image and the same nothing behind the surface.
examples: a novel with flat celluloid characters

entries.definition: (used of color) artificially produced; not natural
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The blankest of these — the colour was put there, with no hint of how or how deep.

entries.definition: (used of color) artificially produced; not natural
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The British spelling, identical in force to *colored*: applied colour, stated without comment.

entries.definition: using artistic forms and conventions to create effects; not natural or spontaneous
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The British spelling, carrying exactly the measured, analytic weight of *conventionalized*.

entries.definition: using artistic forms and conventions to create effects; not natural or spontaneous
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Says the form was settled by convention rather than felt in the moment — cool and analytic, a shortfall of spontaneity rather than of substance.
